questions.questionText: Capitalism lacks -
questions.questionTextEn: Capitalism lacks -
questions.explanation: Capitalist system refers to the method of conducting economic activities under which there is individual ownership of the means of production and freedom to use them for personal gain. It also determines which items should be produced by means, in what quantity and what should be the method of production for maximum satisfaction of their needs? When it is decided independently on the basis of individual market mechanism (powers of demand and supply) and not under any central planning, then it is called capitalist system. In this system, there is no ownership of the state on the means of production, nor does the state interfere in the operation of economic activities. In the capitalist economic system, the consumer is called the king.

questions.questionText: In a socialist society
questions.questionTextEn: In a socialist society
questions.explanation: Among the main features of socialism, all the means of production are collectively under the control of the state, this system is not driven by the motivation of profit but by the spirit of service, the work of production is on the basis of a central planning, the national Efforts are made to distribute the produced wealth on the basis of equality. According to Pigou, "It is impossible to conceive of socialism in any form other than centralized planning." Schumpeter described four qualities of the socialist system - 1. More productivity is determined only in the management of the state. 2. Greater economic welfare due to less inequality. 3. Absence of monopolistic practices. 4. Absence of business cycles.

questions.questionText: Marshall's concept of consumer saving assumes–
questions.questionTextEn: Marshall's concept of consumer saving assumes–
questions.explanation: The French economist dupuit was the exponent of the concept of consumer saving. Marshall explained consumer's savings with the help of cardinal analysis and Hicks with the help of indifference curves. Marshall used the law of diminishing marginal utility to explain the saving of the consumer. According to Marshall, the difference between the price that a person is prepared to pay for a thing and the price that he actually pays, instead of not receiving it, is called the saving of the consumer. Saving of the consumer = total utility derived from the commodity – Total utility sacrificed in the form of money spent on that commodity. According to Hicks, the saving of the consumer should be measured in terms of his income saved. Hicks said that the consumers savings is the amount of money that must be given to or taken away from the consumer after some change in his economic condition, so that the consumer either rises or falls and the same indifference curve but remain as it was before such a change.
questions.explanationEn: The French economist dupuit was the exponent of the concept of consumer saving. questions.questionText: At what point is the equilibrium of firm in the long run under perfect competition?
questions.questionTextEn: At what point is the equilibrium of firm in the long run under perfect competition?
questions.explanation: – In order to attain equilibrium in the long run under perfect competition, the following conditions must be satisfied. (i) Price (P) = Marginal cost (MC) (ii) Price (P) = Average cost (AC) If price is equal to both marginal and average cost then we get the following conditions. Price = marginal cost = Average Cost Since , Marginal cost is. equal only at the lowest print of the average cost curve Therefore, the condition of long run equilibrium of the firm can be written as follows- Price = Marginal cost = lowest Average cost. or, P = LMC = LAC
questions.explanationEn: – In order to attain equilibrium in the long run under perfect competition, the following conditions must be satisfied. (i) Price (P) = Marginal cost (MC) (ii) Price (P) = Average cost (AC) If price is equal to both marginal and average cost then we get the following conditions. questions.questionText: Which of the following is an economic method of development not deterministic?
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is an economic method of development not deterministic?
questions.explanation: Economic growth refers to the increase in real income in an economy over a period of time generally speaking if there is an increase in gross national product gross domestic product income then we say that economic growth is taking place. The concept of economic development is more comprehensive than the concept of economic growth economic growth is related to the growth of production while economic development is social cultural economic qualitative and is related to all quantitative changes. Where economic growth is related to quantitative changes economic growth is related to both quantitative and qualitative changes economic development will be called only when the quality of life improves. It is believed that the per capita income index does not accurately reflect the quality of life so money variables are included in the measurement of economic development such as changes in the form of economic political and social institutions education and literacy rate life expectancy level of nutrition health services per capita durable consumption goods etc.
